anatomy.flutter: Empty/EmptyHeader/EmptyMedia/EmptyTitle/EmptyDescription/EmptyContent, six StatelessWidgets. Empty.build wraps children in a Padding(EdgeInsets.all(padding)) + Column with a radius field (Radii.xl) that is documented as shaping nothing: 'it shapes nothing at present (drift 8: there is no border to shape and no background to clip)'. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The Flutter file's own doc comment ('DRIFT 8 — the dashed border never paints') describes an EARLIER state of empty.tsx that carried only `border-dashed` with no width class, so Preflight zeroed the border and nothing painted; the Flutter widget was ported to match that (no BoxDecoration.border at all, only the radius kept 'for the day a width is added'). The current empty.tsx (read above) already carries a plain `border` class alongside `border-dashed`, so a real 1px dashed rim IS painted on web today. Flutter's Empty paints no border at all. The two are no longer visually equivalent: Flutter is missing the dashed frame the current web renders. states.flutter: Empty and its parts are all StatelessWidget with no controller, no gesture handling and no async lifecycle — there is exactly one render shape per instance, decided entirely by the caller's children.
states.web: The doc page's own States section states: 'Empty is not a control and has no async lifecycle of its own... The interaction and async states below are N/A for that reason,' listing rest/empty as the only real state and hover/focus/pressed/disabled/loading/success as N/A.
states.note: Both sides deliberately declare the same non-interactive, single-shape contract; n/a applies identically on both, so there is nothing to diverge on — recorded per the brief's rule that n/a still needs a note saying why.

disabled.flutter: No `enabled`/`disabled` field or Disabled() wrapper appears anywhere in empty.dart; Empty composes only structural children.
disabled.web: empty.tsx defines no disabled styling or data-disabled attribute anywhere in the file, and the doc page's Accessibility section frames Empty as static content with 'no role or live region of its own'.
disabled.note: Empty is not an actionable control on either platform, so a disabled path does not apply to it; any affordance placed inside EmptyContent (e.g. a Button) carries its own disabled state, audited on that component's own page, not here.
